issues.text: The 200 comes from Ok(...), not from ToDto; ToDto only builds the OrderDto (OrdersController.cs:96, :126-131). The sentence credits the status code to the wrong call.
issues.fix: Change to: "later the result becomes `200` with an `OrderDto`, through `Ok(ToDto(order))`."

issues.text: q1 explanation b (en+vi) says the controller "only translates HTTP", which the reworded summary line 4 now contradicts (the controller also asks for access checks; Create also looks up the caller's customer row). Key and option status are unaffected.
issues.quote: But the controller only translates HTTP, and any other caller of `PlaceOrderAsync` would skip the check.
issues.fix: Replace "the controller only translates HTTP" with "the controller decides no rule about an order's data" (vi: "controller không quyết định quy tắc nào về dữ liệu của đơn").

issues.text: "second access check": I paused to work out what the first one is. For shipping it was StaffOnly, but cancelling does not use StaffOnly, so "second" reads as if cancel runs two checks. It is clear once I reach OrderOwnerHandler, but the word sent me back one paragraph.
issues.quote: Cancelling adds a second access check.
issues.fix: Replace with "Cancelling uses a different access check, `OrderOwnerHandler`."
